title: From Automation to Insight
summary: Automator collects data — Analyst asks questions; numbers alone do not provide insight.

sections.heading: Orientation
sections.subtitle: Introduction to the Lesson
sections.contentMarkdown:
- What will you understand? Having numbers is not the same as knowing what to do with them — Data is just the beginning, not the end.
- Why now? Automator collects data automatically. The Analyst turns it into decisions. Even a simple table or Dashboard is enough to get started.
- What after the lesson? You will choose one table, dashboard, or report — and write down what decision you want to make from it.

sections.heading: Tension
sections.subtitle: A Familiar Situation
sections.contentMarkdown:
- A Dashboard has 20 charts. You open it daily and say, "Looks good" — but nothing has changed in your work because of it.
- The data has become decoration — not a decision-making tool. Automator has increased the pile, but without a specific question, you won’t know how to act.
- AI (artificial intelligence) helps you formulate questions and summarize numbers — you decide which question is worth your time and what decision you will make.

sections.heading: Core Idea
sections.subtitle: The Core Idea
sections.contentMarkdown:
Automator collects — Analyst asks - The Builder created the product — every click and every request is recorded. The Creator brought Reach — every view and every lead is saved.
- Automator brought all of this together in one place: CRM, Sheet, or database.
- The Analyst stands in front of the data and asks: What is working? What is not working? What decision should I make this week?
- Numbers alone are not Insight — Insight appears when your question leads you to an actionable decision.

sections.heading: Comparison
sections.subtitle: A Real-Life Example
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Just looking | Asking a question |
|-----------|------------|
| You open the sales report every morning — see the numbers and move on — no question, no decision | "Why did Conversion drop by 5% this week?" — you open the report with one question, come out with a specific decision, and implement it today |

sections.heading: Glossary
sections.subtitle: Two Terms to Start
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|---------|--------|------|
| Data | Collected numbers and facts — sales, visits, requests | "I sold 45 items this week" — a number, no decision |
| Insight | Understanding that tells you what to do — not just a number on the screen | "Sales increase on Fridays — I will increase advertising on Thursdays" — Insight that changes a decision |

sections.heading: Quiz
sections.subtitle: Quick Confirmation
sections.contentMarkdown:
Question: You noticed that many customers add products to their cart but do not purchase. What is the best first question for the data?
Where exactly do customers drop off in the purchase process (funnel drop-off)?
Explanation: A specific question identifies "where the problem is" — leading you to a decision about the purchase path. General numbers are not enough.

sections.heading: Mission
sections.subtitle: Choose One Source — and Define Your Decision
sections.contentMarkdown:
Introduction: Practical guidance — not complex analysis. Choose one table, dashboard, or report (even a simple Sheet). Write down what decision you want to make from it. Submission: (1) Source · (2) Decision in one sentence · (3) One specific question that the data should answer · (4) If you answered now — what would you do? Evaluation Criteria: | Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-------|-------|---------|
| Clear Decision | 60% | A specific decision — not just "I see the numbers" |
| Relevant Question | 40% | The question is related to the decision — if answered, you know how to act |

sections.heading: Confidence Close
sections.subtitle: What Do You Have Now?
sections.contentMarkdown:
- I understand: Having numbers ≠ knowing what to do — the Analyst asks before opening any report.
- You can: One source + one decision + one question guides you.
- Next: Turn feelings into questions — "I feel that..." → a question that the data answers.
